speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They are the first environment in which children are nurtured and where they experience love and where values are inculcated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Every parent knows that parenthood has its challenges; yet, every parent also knows the joys it brings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government is consistent in its approach to supporting couples and, as couples embark on their parenting journey, we are here to support them and their family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have consistently reviewed our policies over the years to strengthen family ties, particularly between parent and child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: But we recognise that family formation is a personal decision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our measures can only go so far as to address practical obstacles or financial concerns that many parents worry about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: An overall eco-system, which includes family members, community partners, employers and Government measures, is needed to support parents on their journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We remain committed to encouraging people to get married, have children and to raise them in strong families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Child Development Co-Savings Act (CDCA) was first introduced in 2001.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Over the years, we have increased coverage and introduced new schemes under the CDCA as part of a holistic suite of measures that families can tap on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The CDCA now covers the Child Development Account (CDA) and parental leave schemes, with respect to citizen children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Many today will know the CDA as part of the commonly known Baby Bonus scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In 2008, the CDCA was amended to extend maternity leave from 12 weeks to 16 weeks, childcare leave from two to six days and to introduce six days of unpaid infant care leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In 2013, one week of shared parental leave and paternity leave were introduced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We kept in mind that the economy could evolve and support could be extended to a wider group of parents, including those not on regular employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Hence, the Government-Paid Maternity Benefits scheme was introduced for mothers who were either employed or self-employed, but not for the minimum continuous three-month period to qualify for maternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These mothers could be on short-term contracts, or on contracts which expired just before they gave birth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In 2017, we also made it mandatory for employers to grant two weeks of Paternity Leave and increased Shared Parental Leave from one week to up to four weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As a whole, working couples today can take up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave in the child's first year, comprising 16 weeks of maternity leave, two weeks of paternity leave and six days of childcare leave per parent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is the result of continuous policy reviews over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have also made enhancements on other fronts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is in addition to the CDA First Step Grant of $3,000 introduced in 2016 that is paid into the CDA when it is opened, without parents having to contribute first.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The environment that Singaporeans work, live and raise families in, has evolved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF has proposed amendments to the CDCA to bolster our support for citizen children and their working parents, as well as employers, in this changing environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We continue to encourage parenthood within marriage and our proposed amendments also ensure that our operational processes are robust and that there is accountability over public monies even as additional benefits are included and extended.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I now draw the House's attention to the key components in the Child Development Co-Savings (Amendment) Bill, of which there are seven.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As announced in February this year, we will be introducing two new schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Some working fathers and adoptive mothers may not qualify for paternity leave or adoption leave under the CDCA respectively owing to their employment arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They may be on multiple short-term contracts, or had their contracts expire shortly before the birth or adoption of their child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Already, working mothers can be eligible for the existing Government-Paid Maternity Benefits scheme, or GPMB in short, and we are extending this to working fathers and adoptive mothers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Adoptive parents can benefit from GPPB and GPAB if their application to adopt a child is submitted to the Court on or after 1 January 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the case of a foreign child, we will refer to the date on which the dependant's pass is issued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With the new schemes, parents can receive a cash benefit in lieu of the Government-paid portion of paternity leave or adoption leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The parent must have worked as an employee or self-employed person, or both, for at least 90 days in the 12 months immediately preceding the child's date of birth or the eligibility date for an adopted child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The total cash pay-out will be calculated based on the average income earned in the same 12-month period, as prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Therefore, parents who work for longer periods will receive a higher benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Though this number is small, it remains important to ensure that these parents are supported in raising their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Two, assisting parents whose contracts expire, or who are retrenched.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Even as we introduce the new GPPB and GPAB schemes, they are not intended to replace the existing schemes for paternity leave and adoption leave respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Generally, these schemes are mutually exclusive and parents will not be able to qualify for both leave and benefit schemes simultaneously.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The majority of parents will qualify under the relevant leave schemes as they remain employed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The CDCA allows for a GPMB top-up to be given to a mother whose contract expires while she is on maternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: An eligible mother may have started her maternity leave, but could not consume all of it before her contract expired due to the lack of time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Such mothers can receive cash benefits for the remaining Government-paid portion of the leave, which the Government would have reimbursed their employers had the leave not been forfeited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With the new GPAB and GPPB schemes, we will extend this to working fathers and adoptive mothers in similar situations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They, too, will be eligible for a benefits top-up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: My Ministry has also proposed to introduce an additional exception, to assist working parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We know that some parents may be retrenched, and have to give up their remaining leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This leave would also have been otherwise forfeited.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This will help provide greater assurances to parents, as we know that retrenchments are beyond their control.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These protections are provided for under the Employment Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Employers will have to pay maternity leave benefits to pregnant employees who have worked for their employers for at least three months, if their employment is terminated without sufficient cause, or if they are retrenched at any stage of their pregnancy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is an offence to dismiss employees while they are on maternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is also an offence for employers to withhold parental leave from working parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We appreciate that many employers have been voluntarily granting paid leave to such parents as employers play a key role in fostering family-friendly workplaces in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Generally, we have supported this by granting reimbursement to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Bill will now entitle parents of stillborn children to the relevant schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Parents of stillborn children need to recover physically and emotionally and this move can help them in these difficult times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government-paid portion of certain schemes also vary with the number of live citizen children a mother has; these are the maternity and adoption leave and benefit schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For instance, mothers with one or two children who are eligible for maternity leave receive eight weeks of employer-paid leave and eight weeks of Government-paid leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: From the third child, all 16 weeks of maternity leave under the CDCA are paid for by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Depending on whether they are entitled to leave or benefits schemes, including them in the child order determination will allow more employers and working mothers to receive a higher quantum of reimbursement or payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We hope that this will go some way to help mothers and also encourage employers to be more supportive of working mothers with more children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Four, reimbursement to employers who voluntarily grant leave to employees for parental leave schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Employers are one of our main partners in developing a Singapore that is Made for Families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The support from employers is crucial, especially when their employees take on new roles as parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I am heartened to say that many employers have gone the extra mile and allowed employees to benefit from the parental leave schemes, even if the employees have not worked the minimum of three months continuously preceding the birth or adoption of their child to qualify for leave, which is one of the eligibility criteria under CDCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that progressive employers play an important part in helping working parents who are also new to their companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To this end, clauses 10(b), 17(b) and 28(b) give the Government the discretion to reimburse employers if they grant paid maternity leave, paternity leave and adoption leave, respectively, even though the three-month criterion under CDCA is not satisfied.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The parent must still meet all other eligibility criteria mentioned in the Bill, such as having a child who is a Singapore Citizen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I must emphasise that there is no change to a parent’s entitlement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Legislatively, the minimum work criterion is there as a safeguard for employers who also bear some costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, some employers provide leave for employees out of goodwill and can continue to do so of their own volition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The amendments are only intended to give my Ministry more latitude to reimburse these progressive employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Over the years, significant steps have been taken to ensure that every child is cared for and supported in his or her development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The CDCA was last amended to extend maternity leave and the CDA, including the CDA First Step Grant and matched co-savings from the Government, to single unwed parents in 2017 and 2016 respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Earlier in 2013, we had also extended paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave under CDCA to support parents in their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our approach is to enable all Singaporean children and their parents to receive Government benefits that are intended to support the children’s growth and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, the desired social norm in Singapore remains parenthood within marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, we have found that parents could also consume childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave with respect to children born as a result of extramarital affairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our marriage and parenthood policies are intended to safeguard the family institution and not to condone extramarital affairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Gestational mothers will retain their entitlement to paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave to avoid unduly compromising a child’s well-being, given that mothers are, usually, the main caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If the birth parents subsequently marry, the father will become eligible for childcare leave in respect of the child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: All other single unwed fathers whose children are not born out of extramarital affairs continue to be eligible for paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I mentioned earlier that parents will not be able to qualify for both leave and benefit schemes simultaneously, with certain exceptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clause 8(l) will ensure that this treatment is equally applied to both mothers of children who are citizens from birth and those who are new citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To elaborate, mothers of non-citizen children can qualify for maternity leave under the Employment Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Should the child subsequently gain citizenship within one year of the child’s birth, a mother could then qualify for GPMB under CDCA, if she meets the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In contrast, a mother of a citizen child would not be able to receive both paid leave and benefits simultaneously under CDCA, except in certain cases, as earlier mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The proposed amendment will ensure parity between different groups of working mothers, such that those in similar circumstances benefit equally from the maternity leave and benefits provisions under CDCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: First, the amendments will give my Ministry power to carry out audits, or require audits to be conducted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Second, we will expand our powers to recover erroneous payments through clauses 6 and 30.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our powers to clawback are, currently, limited to payments made by mistake of fact, or due to false or misleading information or documents furnished.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government will also be able to deduct the amount from subsequent claims with respect to the same parent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For CDA benefits, the Government may deduct or set off the amount to be recovered from future Baby Bonus benefits payable to the relevant child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will also be able to recover directly from persons who caused the erroneous payments and clawback from CDA trustees or approved persons in the event of unauthorised withdrawals from the CDA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Just as benefits have been progressively expanded over the years, checks and balances must also correspondingly be updated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These amendments ensure that we continue to exercise rigorous oversight over the various schemes provided for under CDCA and bolster accountability over how public monies are utilised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are committed to this cause and have worked to ensure that our policies keep pace with and reflect our desired values.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We want to ensure that parents are supported in their journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, the Government cannot be alone in doing so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Legislation is an insufficient and blunt tool for policies to support parents in child-raising, as families have differing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Equally important are employers, who can create conducive environments for employees to work and have their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are glad to see many have implemented family-friendly practices and I urge others to follow their lead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, the extended family and the community can also pitch in to support families, especially when they are bringing up young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: My Ministry will continue to work with our community partners, such as the Families for Life (FFL) movement so that strong family relations can be fostered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A whole-of-society effort is required, and we will continue to support Singaporeans in this journey.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The proposed amendments are, indeed, helpful in filling the gaps, especially in the current business environment where job losses and business uncertainty are commonplace.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Today, I will speak about my thoughts on benefits for retrenched parents, support for parents of stillborn children, followed by support for pro-family employers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Firstly, I would like to state that I empathise with parents who have babies or young children while struggling with loss of income and uncertainty due to retrenchment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have encountered several cases among my residents who are parents and not long after having their child, lose their jobs; and the family has to scramble to seek financial support.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such situations are daunting because families would not have expected this unfortunate loss of employment to happen.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is especially difficult for mothers, who will experience a lot of anxiety as well as social and emotional trauma due to concerns, such as how they will be able to provide food or milk to their newborn babies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even if they are able to find short-term contract jobs, there is a lot of uncertainty in the current market whereby some of them quickly find themselves out of a job after a few weeks or even after a few days.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are many business owners and self-employed persons who are also experiencing problems.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They may find their incomes cut drastically or they may fall into debt and have to close their businesses for an indefinite period.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In such situations, many families are not entitled to normal leave benefits that comes with a conventional permanent employment contract.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The enhancement of benefits for fathers is, certainly, the right move to improve gender equality.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I would like to ask if this can be brought forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, this will provide some relief to parents who are feeling anxious and, secondly, this will lower the possibility of confusion amongst parents who take the effort to apply and then realise that it is not yet open for application.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister elaborate what is the process for affected parents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What kind of documents and evidence will they have to provide, if any?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think the Minister of State provided some details earlier, but further details might be useful, especially for the man in the street.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What happens if the company they work for is winding up?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How do the claimants secure the relevant HR records?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, these are specific details that I am asking for.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a common problem that when the office is in somewhat of a mess, it will be challenging to retrieve records.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If the company is unable or unwilling to provide the required information, even going as far as to cut off contact, what can the affected parties do to be eligible for their entitled grants?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think that gig workers and freelancers like delivery riders should fall under this category.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, a number of residents are telling me that they are quite doubtful, because they do not have employment contracts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A number of them have only started working as delivery riders this year as a last resort, so, they have not filed their income tax returns either.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This group, generally, also tends to be the hardest hit, because their earnings are directly dependent on the number of hours worked.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If they take a break to tend to childcare needs and if a COVID-19 situation closes down a specific childcare, then they miss all the earnings for that timeframe.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share if they get any entitlements?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And what is their recourse if they do not?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But many after-birth healthcare expenses for both mother and child require money.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Not only that, but the costs for transport to and from the clinics and hospitals as well as special nutrition for mum and baby all add up.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When families are in a stressful situation, the mother, and, sometimes, even the father, too, are prone to post-natal depression, which presents another set of challenges.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, it is important to keep the processes to receive financial grants and aid simplified without compromising governance, so that the applicant would not be put to more stress having to answer a whole gamut of questions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even the need to get a Notary Public to sign off a document can be a challenge as it means having to find their office, travel to and from the lawyer’s office, showing the original documents for inspection and, finally, paying for the fees.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is indeed very thoughtful that we are extending the birth-linked leave and benefits to these parents as they work towards recovering physically and emotionally.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Ministry would also consider subsidising a quantum of any counselling services that the parents may need to undergo to overcome their distress.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This would also, hopefully, go some ways towards normalising the need to seek help for one’s mental health.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These are very challenging times and many have already found their mental health to be affected by the pandemic which has lasted more than a year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To experience the death of a loved one on top of all these problems is nothing short of devastating.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A group of people that we really need empathy from is employers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Pro-family employers are crucial in shaping a nation and culture that are sensitive and encouraging to the needs of parents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the years, the Government has ramped up its policies and expanded the pool of parents who are eligible for paid parental leave.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Employers who do their part to support nation-building and child-rearing must continue to be lauded.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, there are some employers and recruiters who still believe that high productivity is only possible when work is not disrupted.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They want to hire the employee who takes as little leave as possible.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Last month, my colleagues and I moved our Adjournment Motion on workplace discrimination.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My colleague Mr Louis Ng spoke about how some women were passed over for job opportunities simply because they were mothers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But all this means little if employers are passing over parents, especially mothers, for job and promotion opportunities to begin with.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Under normal circumstances, when the economy is prosperous and the labour market is tight, it is easy to say that employers with poor employee welfare policies will find themselves penalised with greater difficulty to hire and retain talent.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Unfortunately, more people are seeking employment than before.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am concerned that improving employees’ welfare may take a backseat for some employers, although this really should not be the case.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Government can do more to reward companies that are genuinely pro-family.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Government already offers leave benefits and reimbursements, as well as grants to cultivate family-friendly workplace polices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We all know there are many long-term benefits when companies have engaged and happy workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Unfortunately, many are more interested in quick fixes, especially with the current pandemic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, even if they are essentially funded to redesign their company policies, they may feel the effort is not worthwhile.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And, likewise, it would be a temporary move, so, when the economy improves and the employer is able to see for themselves that the effort of implementing family-friendly policies pays off in the long run, they would have an existing system in place and will be inclined to continue with it even without external rewards.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For those who go ahead to have children, the poor economy has made parenthood a greater struggle, on top of other social distancing measures that have greatly disrupted play time and the social lives of our young ones.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is prudent to have support measures so that our current generation of little ones may at least have a happy and healthy early childhood.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Many of the proposed changes extend support to those who are either enduring an incalculable loss or taking on an enormous responsibility, as they undertake sacrifices to secure the next generation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As a society, we should absolutely help them in any way we can.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will speak today about the importance of helping the dejected, downtrodden and disaffected: parents of stillborn children, parents who have adopted children and working women in a precarious position due to a pregnancy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: At that time, I was 13 and my sister, six.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Since our family was of modest means, my mother had to contribute to the household with a full-time job, which meant that she encountered all the challenges that working mothers face when they are working and carrying a child at the same time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Moreover, it was a difficult pregnancy because mom was already more advanced in her years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In the final months, I recall how she had to sleep upright on many nights due to the discomfort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But we took the fact that since the expected birth would occur exactly seven years apart from my sister's and 14 after mine – seven being the perfect number – as a sign that my brother's conception was a gift from God.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In the early hours of 6 May, I awoke to my father’s presence in my bedroom.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: He had tears in his eyes, one of only three times in my life when I had seen him cry. “We lost Jaaron,” he said.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The sign of the seven had not been that perfect, after all.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It took my mother at least that many years to recover from that loss.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Along the way, she questioned her choices, her faith and herself.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Consequently, I believe that we should not exempt the latter from any of the benefits of rest and recovery that Government-mandated maternity leave confers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If anything, the added psychological trauma that the latter will experience may even be the cause for being willing to think about extending even longer maternity leave periods for such individuals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Since the norm in Singapore is either 12 weeks of maternity leave or 16 weeks of Government-paid maternity leave, it would not be unreasonable to allow for a longer leave period for those who have to recover from not just physical but also mental wounds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As I shared earlier, the loss of my brother was one of only three occasions when I had seen my father cry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: He was a traditional man and not given to public expression of his emotions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But the fact that he mourned the loss of my brother is indicative of the sort of pain and anguish that fathers also go through when they experience the loss of a child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Consequently, it would make eminent sense for compassionate leave to be extended to the father in the case of a stillborn child, too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: At this point, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I will return to the example of my mother.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I seem to be talking a lot about my mother; it is something that she would, undoubtedly, find great delight in and I see this as simply payback, since she never seems to tire about talking about her children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As it turns out, my mother was also adopted as a child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This made an immense difference to her life, especially since my grandfather passed on while she was still a very young girl, and the fact that my mother was but one of 10 children meant that it was impossible for my grandmother to have raised her on her own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Adoption confers a lease of life for such children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Adoption is a gift of parenthood for those who might, for various reasons, be unable to have biological children of their own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As every forever parent knows, there is absolutely no distinction between being a parent to a biological or an adoptive child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It stood at 1.1 per female in 2020.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Clause 13 is, therefore, a wholly welcome recognition of this reality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: However, I should point out that the language in which the amendments are embedded – that the adoption benefits apply to eligible mothers – automatically vests these benefits onto the adoptive mother.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Even the proposed addition of section 12A(4)(b) does not fully offset this implicit bias, since it still requires the mother to elect to share these benefits, in accordance with section 12(E)(5) of the original Act, with the father.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Moreover, while uncommon, the Adoption of Children Act does allow single men to adopt children, just not girls, except under very special circumstances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Clause 8(e) of the Bill introduces amendments to section 9A of the Act that are designed to protect working mothers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This House will, inevitably, return to this theme as we debate the gender equality Motion tomorrow.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Here, I will limit my comments to underscoring how important it is to protect female employees who become pregnant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Too often, we hear stories from our female friends and residents about how they are burdened by an immense sense of insecurity after they become pregnant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In some egregious cases, however, unscrupulous employers may advance a case based on structural reasons to release a pregnant employee.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While it is very difficult for an external party to perfectly adjudicate the validity of such justifications, per se, the fallback of Government-provided maternity benefits is, surely, welcome, as an additional safety net.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: On a parting note, I would like to touch just very briefly on the issue of returns on savings in CDAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Here, my concern is one of omission, rather than commission.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: There were notably no amendments proposed to CDCA pertaining to returns on CDAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Indeed, beyond a brief allusion to returns on CDAs in the original Co-savings Scheme, which states that it seeks, and I quote, "to facilitate the making of financial provision for the development of a child… through the making of contributions to the child’s bank account", in section 3 of the original Act, along with some notion of the protection of benefits in section 5, there is remarkably little guidance on returns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, while CDAs do receive a number of Government grant injections and dollar-for-dollar matches, the incentives to further contribute to co-saving into the account – an aspiration embedded right in the name of the Act – is hardly encouraged.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As Members of this House will undoubtedly be aware, the closest we have to magic in the world of finance is the power of compound interest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Notwithstanding these additional remarks, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is only right that the Government formalises the arrangement to reimburse employers who voluntarily grant parental leave to employees and make provisions for audits and recovery of erroneous payments.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to take this opportunity to make a request for parents of multiple births.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Parents do not receive double or additional Government-paid benefits.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, many countries already offer additional benefits to parents of multiple births.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They include European countries and our neighbours in North and Southeast Asia.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that the Government will consider giving these parents more benefits so that they can have more time to take care of their babies, have a good rest and make further efforts to have a few more.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would be helpful in encouraging more births, too.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): I would like to take this opportunity to make a request on behalf of parents of multiple births.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a small group of parents but we must try to help them as much as possible.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Multiple births are a blessing but coping with twins, triplets or more babies is extremely challenging, especially for new mothers, and most of these will be new mothers because Singaporeans are having fewer babies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Presently, the birth of twins or multiple babies is treated as a single delivery.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The parents will not receive double or additional benefits.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While the parents can receive the benefits for a subsequent delivery, due to our low fertility rate, once a family has two or more children, the chance for a subsequent delivery may not be high.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, why do we not provide more benefits for such families?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The parents will be better rested and, instead of feeling stressed and overwhelmed, might be encouraged to have another child or more children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As it is, many other countries are already offering parents of multiple births additional benefits.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They range from European countries to our neighbours in North and Southeast Asia.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If the concern is the impact on employers, the impact is very small.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Flexibility and mutual understanding between employers and employees are key.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Ministry will consider my request favourably.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It expands support to a wider group of working parents and promotes a more family-friendly working environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The roles of working parents are already challenging in the best of times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Any support is even more welcomed in challenging times like the present pandemic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I am supportive of the measures of this Bill, I sincerely hope we can amend this piece of legislation further and provide more support to more parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first suggestion is about leave benefits where to-be parents suffer a miscarriage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am supportive of the move in this Bill to provide birth-linked leave and benefits to parents of stillborn children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a compassionate policy which recognises the need for these parents to recover both physically and emotionally.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While a stillborn child is defined as a child who is birthed after the 28th week of pregnancy, the event is no less traumatic for parents where a mother miscarries in the 27th week of pregnancy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, these mothers are not eligible for maternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOM's guidance instead states that these others may take sick leave to recover.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, suffering a miscarriage is very different from coming down with the flu.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also the mother who is entitled to sick leave to recover physically.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The reality is that these parents, both mother and father, may require time to recover together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill extends support to parents, including working fathers, adoptive mothers on short-term employment contracts, retrenched parents and parents with stillborn children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, if it is difficult to be a working parent, single unwed working parents have an even heavier burden of filling the shoes of both parental figures both emotionally and financially.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government's stance towards single unwed parents has evolved and I am appreciative of this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2019, then Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling, in response to my Adjournment Motion, said, "Single unwed parents and their children are valued citizens in our society, and like all parents, are respected for the love and care they provide for their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are no less a mother or a father, just because their child was born outside of marriage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their children, like any other children in our society, are precious and every parent, regardless of their marital status, ought to be treated with respect.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I acknowledge that in the past, the Government was fairly strict in limiting public housing access to married couples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For single unwed parents, we hope to facilitate their efforts to build a stable environment for their child." Indeed, we have made much progress.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We already provide them with the CDAC component of the Baby Bonus.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have levelled the playing field in terms of maternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The cash component of the Baby Bonus will go a long way in helping single unwed parents build a stable environment for their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many single unwed parents need the cash component more than parents in dual-income families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are asking to be treated fairly and equally.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope that the Ministry will review this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members of this House will be no stranger to my daughters Ella, Katie and Poppy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some Members tell me that they wait for me to say their names in my speeches.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have shared many of their stories in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All these stories come from the memories I have forged with them through time spent together, precious time, especially when they were little babies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I took my paternity leave, treasured it and wished I had more time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My factory is closed, so, I would never get paternity leave again, as Ms Joan Pereira has said, when you have twins, you will never have more kids.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I know how important this leave is and I want to make sure fathers have previous time with their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have said this many times: "Spend time with those you love, one of these days, you will either say I wish I had or I am glad I did." Study after study show that paternity leave is vital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, children whose fathers took paternity leave have fewer behavioural problems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These findings were similar to an IPS research paper in 2019 that found that fathers who took paternity leave experienced reduced conflicts, stronger family relationships and increased satisfaction in their marriage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What message do we send out when we give mothers 16 weeks of maternity leave and fathers two weeks of paternity leave?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The IPS research paper stated that, "Family policies in Singapore continue to signal that childcare is a woman's responsibility and reinforce gender stereotypes." Indeed, they do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can introduce the increases to paternity leave in phases, giving our employers time to plan ahead, while also providing a clear signal of our intentions to reduce the gender stereotype around parenting.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Minister of State will look into this proposal in consultation with the relevant stakeholders, including the tripartite partners and NGOs, such as Families for Life and Centre for Fathering.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the amendments have significant effects on many families and all employers, I am sure many would applaud the amendments in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am also equally sure that many would have constructive feedback that would have helped refine the Bill further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And we all need to remember the advice that Minister Vivian Balakrishnan gave us, "Life is a one-way ticket.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A baby will only remain a baby for a very short time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They will grow up before we even realise it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The thing about life is we cannot rewind time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, my advice to young parents here is, your children need you, they need you desperately and they need you only for a very, very transient time in their lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we miss it, we cannot get it back." Madam, notwithstanding the above points, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The key message in this Bill is that the Government stands ever-ready to support couples in starting families and having children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Bill also signals a continuing shift from the traditional notion of mothers being primary caregivers to children, emphasising the role of fathers in parenthood.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, the extension of benefits to parents of a stillborn child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There have been calls from various organisations to legitimise stillbirths as a significant life event.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many jurisdictions, such as the UK, have related policies to support women through stillbirth pregnancies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The trauma of stillbirth pregnancies cannot be understated; not only is there physical trauma, but what we must focus on is the lasting mental trauma it causes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I join Member Saktiandi Supaat in asking for the Government to support greater mental health support for this group of mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The extension of paternity leave and benefits to parents of a stillborn child will go a long way in reassuring couples that the Government acknowledges the mental trauma of stillbirths and will fully support these couples through such adversity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, the pandemic has brought forth many job changes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But structurally, accepting a new job meant that some expectant employees may not be statutorily entitled to maternity benefits if they have worked for less than three months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is a good move to lean into the needs of our mothers and will encourage companies to go beyond short-term considerations and support our mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As the next bound of development, I hope that the Ministry can consider greater support for single mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We have come a long way in our support for single mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In 2016, the extension of maternity leave for single mothers to 16 weeks marked a positive change in our attitudes towards single mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In 2019, MND indicated that all mothers are equal and are welcome to apply for HDB housing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We have, indeed, made headway over the past decade in supporting our single mothers and we must not stop here.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I have spoken about the financial and mental hardships that single mothers face on various occasions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Not only do single mothers have less resources, compared to a two-parent family, but they also face the stigma of being unmarried, with the emphasis on parenthood within marriage in Governmental policies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Under the current framework, single mothers are not entitled to various benefits.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Although extending these benefits to single mothers may seemingly deviate from the traditional definition of a family unit, we must remember that the majority of single mothers are in their position due not to reasons within their control.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Extending benefits, such as the Baby Bonus scheme to single mothers will benefit the child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Children of single mothers are all of equal importance as children of a married couple.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These children all form the future generation of Singaporeans and we must not unduly disadvantage children of single mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I urge the Ministry to consider extending more benefits to single mothers, such as the Baby Bonus scheme and the various reliefs, that single mothers are entitled to.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Notwithstanding the above calls for supporting single mothers, I rise in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I feel that, as a society, we should have a re-think and consider accepting either the wife or the husband as a full-time homemaker looking after children and to waive the requirement of at least three months of work records.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We should recognise that being a homemaker is a job in itself.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, the parental benefits can be given to the homemaker, that means, only one of the parents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Regarding reimbursements to employers who voluntarily grant leave to employees for parental leave, I would like to ask how much reimbursement has been given each year since the scheme was launched.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although there are caps which vary between high- and low-income groups, the costs of leave among staff do differ for employers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What has been the amounts of reimbursement for each income group?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While this is good, middle- and lower-income families may not benefit as much as the higher-income groups, because they may face challenges putting in as much savings.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How do we encourage parents to contribute to their children's CDAs to ensure they are not left out, especially parents who are self-employed and freelancers?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What has been the number of children for each income group which benefited from the scheme?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What has been the total grants for each child in each of the income groups?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many appeals has the Ministry received regarding CDAs?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Yet, with all three come much uncertainty for the Singaporean worker.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With today's reading of the Child Development Co-Savings Bill, we welcome amendments that safeguard the interests of workers and families alike.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This signals that the Government recognises the biodiversity of livelihoods within our eco-system of workers and that alternative forms of livelihoods, such as contract workers, deserve to be weatherproofed, just as permanent employees' are.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Not only should all workers be protected equally; so should all parents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some believe that parenting begins when a child is born, but I believe that parenthood begins in pregnancy – when your pregnancy home kit test first signals that you are positive, when you hear your child's first heartbeat, when you take your first ultrasound picture of your child.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For a couple, there is so much expectation, so much preparation up to the due date.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For most parents, this due date is a joyous occasion while, for some, a profound pain envelops their expectant hearts.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am referring to parents of stillborn children.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Indeed, there is a physical healing process still for the mother to go through.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But deeper and more unique to such couples is the emotional healing process, as other Members of this House have talked about.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Grieving, accepting and moving on from such a tragedy require plenty of space and time.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These birth-linked leave and benefits are thus appropriately and necessarily conferred on these couples who are very much parents in their own right.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As we celebrate the sensible considerations undergirding the amendments in this Bill that will move us towards more equitable outcomes for families, it is actually of paramount importance that we recall the spirit of the legislation at hand – that is, to support families in having more children.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While, on paper, much of the legislation revolves around financial provisions for parents, these measures shape cultural norms, whether we like it or not.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In particular, I am referring to the way the burden of parenting is shouldered by couples.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, I would like to preface by saying that this is not a call to point fingers, nor a "call out", but rather an invitation to share in the joys of parenting.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: When fathers do not pull their weight in parenting, both miss out on the joys of parenting – fathers from absence or distance and mothers from tiredness or burnout.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Although we may feel our take-up rates are strong against international standards, the actual benchmark for strong take-up rates should instead be compared to the take-up rates of maternity leave at home.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Anything less than equal and we still have work to do.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This, once again, is not to point fingers at fathers – most dads do want to spend time with their kids and many of my residents who are fathers have expressed joy with how much easier this has become since they have been working from home.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We need to pick up our fight with what lies deeper – workplace cultures embedded in our society.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While no employers are hanging signs on office walls discouraging fathers from taking paternity leave, many fathers might feel the threat of being implicitly penalised for taking days off to care for their children.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Perhaps, some employers think that this could be rightfully and naturally left to their spouses, or even see the usage of paternity leave as unnecessary or, worse still, opportunistic.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, it is no longer enough that employers merely provide opportunities for fathers taking paternity leave or other benefits, especially when fathers might be left second-guessing the costs incurred to their careers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Instead, employers should go a step further to actively encourage fathers to take days off to care for their family, especially in the form of their paternity leave days.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is the kind of assurance that is sure to drive the take-up rates of paternity leave usage.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: An example could be expanding the Working Mother's Child Relief and Grandparent Caregiver Relief to working fathers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: By availing incentivisation schemes to both mothers and fathers, this would reflect the better sharing of parental duties, reinforce the positive communications and, indeed, raise the visibility to the important role males play in parenting and, indeed, caregiving.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To go a step further, I draw on two recommendations our Women's Wing and Young PAP have formulated.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This flexible redistribution of the total maternity and paternity leave entitlement pie does not create additional burden to employers who are facing manpower shortages and yet places choice and full control in the hands of the parents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As I have mentioned, not only should all workers be treated fairly; so, also should all parents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We, too, delight in good ideas, but our delight is made complete in ideas that birth action, rather than just laundry lists that are strong on paper but often remain only on paper.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement's continued ability to weave idealism and activation has been a cornerstone for women's consistent elevation in the workforce and we submit these calls to the Government as we march forward in a fruitful partnership.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Stronger families start with healthier parents and healthier parents are those who shoulder each other's burdens willingly and joyfully.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is what a strong family starts with.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.31 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 4.11 pm until 4.31 pm.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It has often been quoted that our greatest resource is our people.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our people drive the economy, forming a skilled and productive workforce in order to remain competitive.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This same workforce must reproduce itself and, at the same time, provide care to our children who will be the workforce of the future.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Today, traditional notions of gender roles have shifted to more women pursuing their aspirations in the workforce while earning to support the family, away from the figure of the sole male breadwinner going out to work while the woman stays home.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With more women participating in the workforce, the dynamics of having a child today are very different from before.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But while the players have changed, the rules of the game have not quite kept up and expectations are still rooted in the past.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is not uncommon to hear women struggling with the mental load, burnt out from caregiving responsibilities, expected to attend that 5.30 pm Zoom work call while preparing dinner for the family and swinging by childcare to pick up the infant.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is still a gender bias in caregiving, something we have repeatedly heard during the ongoing Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development, highlighting a clear demand for greater equality in sharing responsibilities at home.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The monetisation of unused paternity leave under the GPPB provides an option that can benefit our families.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, it may not provide an incentive for parents to shoulder more responsibility at home.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, it may have the unintended consequence of lowering the opportunity cost for fathers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We already have a low take-up rate of paternity leave, with some pointing to societal attitudes, stigma, against men being caregivers as reasons for this, especially in the private sector.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The perfect woman is often imagined to have it all.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I have not yet had the opportunity to be a mom, I remember the daily dilemmas of a former colleague and friend of mine who has three children and, when one child is sick, it can be impossible to find a caregiver or enough days of leave.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the ground, we have heard of parents begging school principals to keep their child in infantcare if it is only a sniffle or light cough, instead of taking the child home, or despairing when a helper or grandparent is suddenly put on a Quarantine Order.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It can be an impossible situation for parents.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a society, we need to adjust both policies and mindsets to encourage fathers to play a more active role in raising their children.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, fathers have two weeks of paternity leave, with the option of "taking" four weeks from their partners.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But despite the Government's ongoing efforts to get men more involved in raising their children, the majority of fathers do not take up the shared leave.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some have expressed reluctance to reduce the leave of the mothers as they read the differential in leave as a signal as to who is more responsible.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: More equal exclusive paternity leave, 16 weeks versus two weeks, will create opportunities for fathers, rather than making couples make tough decisions on a limited number of weeks, as mothers, too, prize the chance to bond with their child.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the future, we can consider varying mechanisms to support wider family structures of fathers or mothers in their caregiving journey.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In Germany, parents can access Parental Allowance Plus, which gives them the right to receive a parental allowance from the government, including if both parents decide to take parental leave at the same time, thus allowing for precious family time instead of foisting the responsibility of caregiving on just one parent.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Spouses or partners who take care of the child after birth, even if the child is not their own, may also receive parental allowance, subject to the same conditions which give greater recognition to different family structures.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This also applies to relatives up to the third degree, if the parents cannot look after their child alone on account of a hardship, such as disability, and also goes beyond adopted parents to include children taken into foster care with the aim of adoption.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that, as society evolves and family structures change, we will be even more inclusive in the definition of the child.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, we also need to recognise associated costs in implementing family-friendly policies, especially for businesses, in particular, SMEs or start-ups, which may struggle to find workers to cover.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Where we can, we should also try to alleviate the cost on businesses.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Incorporating family-friendly policies in our workplace could be positive tools for hiring and employee retention, where employees feel cared for and they can grow with the family through different life stages and are more likely to remain loyal in a good work environment.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a high correlation between employee satisfaction, family-friendly policies and flexibility in work.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
