text: (In Malay):   In several meetings between myself, residents and volunteers in Ang Mo Kio, I have observed a change of mindset among fathers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many of them now share the same responsibilities as mothers in terms of caregiving, providing guidance and spending time with their families.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They show more concern and get involved in the daily chores.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But at the same time, fathers have also shared with me the dilemma they face in balancing their responsibilities as dedicated husbands, fathers and workers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need efforts, not just on the part of the Government, but also from all levels of society, to eradicate the kind of thinking and workplace culture that places more pressure on the role of fathers or mothers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are many companies that can be emulated as inclusive employers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Guidance and support from men are also important in our efforts to encourage women to achieve their career aspirations and their lifelong dreams.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I will not be here today without the support of my father and husband, who help to prepare breakfast or coffee and with the household chores.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I acknowledge that not all women receive the same support and guidance.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that this proposal can transform workplace culture to provide opportunities for parents to progress in their careers without any stigma and dilemma.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that more fathers will step forward to use paternity leave and the time given to help their wives and children in order to foster closer family ties at home.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I am encouraged by the amendments introduced and support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I am especially glad for the enhancements to the Government-Paid Paternity Benefits, as well as the Government's reimbursements to companies which opt to give additional leave to parents beyond the statutory requirements.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It certainly helps in the efforts to encourage workplace cultures to be more family-friendly.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I have a clarification to ask and some suggestions to make.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: First, can there be more transparency and clearer instructions on how Self-Employed Persons' claims for Government-Paid Maternity and Paternity benefits will be assessed?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I have had residents who write in to ask how and what proof they need to submit to show that they have taken leave when they are their own bosses.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This applies to freelancers and sole proprietors who include tuition teachers, coaches, designers, arts and sports instructors, beauticians, home caterers, consultants, marketeers and many others, even including delivery riders, like what my hon colleague, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, has mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They are unsure and confused about what extent of documentation they need to submit and whether their claims will be approved.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It would be helpful to have more clarity and certainty, as the success of the paid leave reimbursements impact on their financials at a time when money could be very tight due to the increased expenses brought on by a newborn child.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Second, amendments must be made for low-income families who currently benefit very little from the dollar-for-dollar matched savings benefit.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And I echo my colleague Mr Gan Thiam Poh's call for it.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Low-income Singaporeans are not able to save much, given their jobs and salaries pay only enough to make ends meet, if at all.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This will be a positive step to help bridge the inequality gap, by providing better for children from low-income households.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: A financial literacy programme tailored to this community can also be coupled with this benefit to help equip low-income families with the planning skills to attain and maximise savings.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I echo and support my hon colleague Mr Louis Ng's call to make unwed parents eligible for the Baby Bonus Cash Gift.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Although I understand the Government's position that it does not want to signal or encourage the birth of children out of wedlock, it needs to recognise that such circumstances can be born out of misfortune and not always wilful promiscuity.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I have a resident who was unable to marry her fiancé after getting pregnant because he died from a traffic accident before their wedding.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: To this day, she still feels penalised from being excluded from the various support schemes, including housing support, due to circumstances beyond her control.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Many unwed mothers may also choose not to be trapped by marriage to irresponsible men.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The fact that these men are irresponsible is often a discovery after the deed.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Marriage is not always the ideal option if the father proves to be an untenable lifelong partner.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: No matter what one's view or value is on wedlock, I believe we can all agree that the child of unwed parents should not be made to suffer the consequences of the parents' choices or mistakes.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If the Government's intention is to discourage extra-marital affairs, I would urge the Government to look into better enforcement of child support payments.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: One possibility could be using DNA tests to identify and hold accountable biological parents.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Accountability to a child whom one sires or births should be regardless of marital status.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This will help unwed mothers caring for a child to access child support payments from their co-parents if necessary.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In the rare case where the one caring for the child is the biological father, the accountability should be equally applied to any mother who has chosen to bail.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Every child born is precious, especially in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I hope CDCA can go beyond being a support programme to encourage and support parenthood to also become an instrument to equalise the circumstances and well-being of every Singaporean child.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In summary, I would like to make three asks.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: One, more administrative clarity for self-employed parents to access paternity and maternity benefits.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Two, differentiated and higher ratio child-development savings match for low-income families.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Three, equalised cash support in Baby Bonus, possibly renamed Baby Support, to children of unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many have to juggle with work-from-home arrangements and, at the same time, help their children with home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For others, they may have been made redundant or experienced a drop in income.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Bill amendments reflect that the Government is aware of parenting challenges during this difficult period.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I will touch on three issues in my speech.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It would not be a stretch to say that single parents are the hardest hit during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They have to juggle managing their children, their jobs and everything else, with little to no support without a spouse.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even if they qualify for maintenance fees, it is a perpetual challenge for some to claim these fees, which involves going to Court each time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: At recruitment interviews, their marital status and caregiving arrangements are a perpetual concern for interviewers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They also do not have sufficient childcare leave or someone else to share the burden.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A resident of mine, a single mother of one child, told me that she has been unemployed for two years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This was because she has been unable to find an employer who would accommodate her need to fulfill her caregiving duties.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Although single parents from low-income households may tap on financial assistance, the application and renewal processes are reportedly tedious.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regardless of their circumstances, these children are Singapore Citizens.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While some employers may not be compassionate enough to allow them to take bereavement leave, suffering a miscarriage is not quite the same as losing a family member to external circumstances.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should acknowledge and empathise that a miscarriage is a devastating life event, which can take a significant toll on one's physical and emotional well-being.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, with more parents and, in turn, employers becoming eligible for the leave benefits, are they required to apply for the grants or will the process be automated?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If manual application is required, can the Ministry share about the application and approval process?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the platforms to apply and to check on applications be made digital and seamless?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For a start, I think applicants should not be required to produce the supporting documents, as the relevant information on employees' marital status, number of children and so on should be available in the Government database.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also an unnecessary inconvenience for the officers processing the applications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Deputy Speaker, as with all new and enhanced initiatives involving finances, there must be effective means to monitor how well they are working.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Government share how we intend to measure success for this initiative?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the KPIs to determine whether more parents are benefiting from family-friendly policies at the workplace?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are we looking beyond the amount of reimbursements issued and leave granted?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I hope we can go beyond counting the figures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should have actual conversations with parents to find out if these measures have boosted their confidence to grow their family in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These measures would be useful to assess if the initiatives have truly translated into family-friendly work environments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a father of five myself, this issue concerns me personally.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am aware that many fathers do not take paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It will spur employers to support more fathers to spend time with their families.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, we hope that fathers will actively take up these entitlements to spend time with their children, as they go through their formative years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nothing should be more important than being there for one's kids when it matters most.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To all Members who have spoken on the Bill, I am grateful for your support of the Bill and the queries raised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Many of us continue to place emphasis on ensuring an environment that supports families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Many Members also recognised that it is a complex task to balance the many interests and considerations at hand when it comes to decisions on whether new policies should be introduced and if enhancements should be made to existing schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some have alluded to the many factors at play and I am glad that they appreciate the balance the Government must strike.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have to safeguard taxpayers' monies and allocate as fairly as we can, knowing that any policy decision made has an indelible impact across multiple stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members, such as Ms Carrie Tan, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Desmond Choo, have suggested that more could be done for single unwed parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I respect their views and I thank Member Louis Ng for sharing what I had said in Parliament before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I had highlighted in my opening speech the suite of measures that all Singaporean children can access.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These include subsidies in healthcare, education, childcare and infant care, as well as the MediSave Grant for Newborns, MediShield Life coverage from birth and the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Concession.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In 2017, we extended support to unwed mothers for maternity leave under the CDCA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For unwed fathers who are the main caregivers of their children, MSF also evaluates their requests for paternity leave on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members have also raised that more benefits could be extended to single unwed parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Single unwed parents who require further help can approach our Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For other benefits, such as the Baby Bonus Cash Gift and parenthood-related tax benefits, these continue to be targeted to encourage parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We acknowledge Members' concerns about single unwed parents and we will do what we can to support them based on their needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also hope to assure Members that, together with other agencies, we regularly review how we can better support them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For single unwed parents who require further support, they can also look to the SPIN programme, which can help improve their access to information and resources.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Carrie Tan shared that there was a need to look into better enforcement of child support payments so as to reiterate that accountability to a child is independent of marital status.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member will be happy to note that the duty of a parent to maintain his or her child is already provided for under the Women's Charter, regardless of whether the child is legitimate or illegitimate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Unwed mothers are, therefore, already able to apply to the Court for maintenance of a child from the father.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Gan Thiam Poh also shared that some low-income parents may not be able to fully maximise the co-matching feature of CDA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This feature first requires parents to deposit into CDA to receive Government co-matching, which may be challenging for some low-income parents who may not have the means to set aside enough to save into CDA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is granted to all Singaporean children, regardless of their parents' marital or income status.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I am glad that some community partners have also stepped forward to help families save more into CDA by making deposits into the accounts of children from low-income families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These contributions will qualify for Government co-matching and we encourage them to continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Government also provides adhoc top-ups to CDA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Therefore, parents have a substantial amount of time to deposit money into CDA to maximise the co-matching caps and should plan to do so at their own pace.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim has asked why there are no legislative provisions to clearly set out the interest rates that apply to CDA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We welcome his wholehearted endorsement of CPF and its very generous, risk-free returns.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: CDA's interest rates are determined by banks but have, generally, been higher than a normal savings account.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On top of this, despite CDA being a bank account, the Government provides co-matching.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Monies in CDA are intended to support the child's growth and development during their early years, in contrast to CPF, which helps support Singaporeans in their retirement years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And parents are able to withdraw from CDA, as needed, to defray educational and healthcare expenses at approved institutions, as compared to CPF.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are dedicated schemes that low-income families can turn to, if they need social assistance, and such families can approach our Social Service Offices (SSOs), which stand ready to render help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our SSOs will assess their households' needs and circumstances and provide assistance accordingly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, families who require support with their basic living expenses can receive ComCare financial assistance if they meet the criteria and SSOs may also refer families to other Government agencies and community partners, such as Family Service Centres, for further support.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked that we consider waiving the employment criterion for Leave and Benefits schemes, in consideration of stay-at-home parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, a cash grant could be given to a stay-at-home parent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Leave and Benefits schemes are meant to support working parents in managing their work and caregiving responsibilities, without having to leave the workforce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, we value the contributions of stay-at-home parents, as they, too, play a fundamental role in nurturing the next generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As such, we have put in place other support schemes that Singaporean children and their families can receive, regardless of their parents' working status, including the Baby Bonus Scheme, the MediSave Grant for Newborns and the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy Concession.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: One of the Government's key priorities is to ensure that parents have access to quality and affordable preschools for their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked about the accessibility of preschool places for parents who have switched to hybrid or remote working.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Going forward, we will continue to build more preschool places in tandem with upcoming HDB developments where there are more new families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA closely monitors local preschool enrolment and availability and regularly reviews its plans.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Should local demand shift and exceed earlier expectations, ECDA would work with preschools and HDB to look into activating more void deck and communal spaces for centre extensions, where available.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members such as Ms Carrie Tan, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Mr Yip Hon Weng, have asked for clarity on the application process and how claims and payouts under the Government-Paid Leave Schemes and Benefits are assessed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In particular, Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Saktiandi Supaat have asked how self-employed persons' leave claims are assessed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Broadly, a self-employed man or woman is a resident of Singapore who engages in or carries on any trade, business, profession or vocation other than employment under a contract of service and derives income from such trade, business, profession or vocation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Freelancers and gig workers fall within this definition, as do delivery drivers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To be clear, self-employed persons can qualify for payment under either the Leave or Benefits schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Their employment arrangement is the one that will determine which scheme they qualify under.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To Ms Carrie Tan's queries on how self-employed parents' leave claims are assessed and Mr Yip Hon Weng's query on whether the application and approval processes are automated, let me illustrate with an example.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Self-employed mothers can submit maternity leave claims at MSF's "profamilyleave" website.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They have to provide basic information, such as their personal particulars and their child's, as well as their occupation and period of inactivity from work.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To avoid over-burdening applicants, we require only critical information to enable assessment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In most cases, they do not need to submit documents at this point of application but are required to declare that the information provided is accurate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have automated the process, as much as possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will verify against available data in the Government database that the eligibility criteria are met, for example, that the applicant's child is a Singapore Citizen.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In determining the amount, we will look at the relevant Notice of Assessment, which is prescribed in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For self-employed parents without a Notice of Assessment, I can assure Members that MSF will consider other documents which can serve as proof of income to facilitate our assessment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These could include bank statements, contracts for services or invoices.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about the application process for the new Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and the Government-Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB) schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked about the application process for parents who have been retrenched but have unconsumed leave and want to apply for a benefits top-up.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Generally, the application process is similar to an application under the existing Government-Paid Maternity Benefits scheme, which is done at MSF's "profamilyleave" website.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Parents will need to submit all their employment contracts for the period of 12 months immediately preceding their child's date of birth or eligibility date for an adopted child and their payslips for the employments or the latest Notice of Assessment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will also need to submit the retrenchment letter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For parents who require more details and fellow Members who meet residents with these queries, I encourage you to visit the "profamilyleave" website, which has information on the eligibility criteria, application procedures and payment for the various schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF is also happy to render assistance to parents who require help in navigating the process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gam Thiam Poh raised a good point that we do not want self-employed persons to be left out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I hope that my explanation will reassure working parents who are self-employed, that they, too, should apply for the Leave and Benefits schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To Mr Gan Thiam Poh's point that the amounts reimbursed to employers or paid out in the form of benefits may vary from person to person, this is correct.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For employees on the leave schemes, they will continue to receive their salaries for the duration of their leave and, for the Government-paid portion, this would be subject to the reimbursement caps.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The more a parent has worked in the 12 months before the birth of the child or eligibility date for an adopted child, the more benefits he or she will be eligible for.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our Leave and Benefits schemes are intended to support bona fide working parents and, therefore, the support granted will differ based on the parents' employment arrangement and economic activity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has also requested for additional data on the various schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While having more data-points will bolster our understanding of family needs, as a general principle, MSF does not require information for claims and applications above and beyond what is necessary to determine eligibility and entitlement.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This avoids burdening employers and working parents excessively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, household income is not needed to determine the quantum of Baby Bonus benefits, as the scheme does not vary with income.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Likewise, we also do not require parents to submit information about the number of children they have when processing claims for Leave and Benefits schemes that do not vary with the birth order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Parents also need not submit information on other grants that they have received.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In this regard, we seek the Member's understanding that we must balance the need for policy review with making our claim and application processes citizen-centric and efficient.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat requested that the GPPB and GPAB application date of 1 December 2021 be brought forward.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I seek the Member's understanding that we require time to make the necessary amendments to subsidiary legislation and to also enhance the IT system to support the schemes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling has suggested a review of current schemes to better reflect the principle of shared parental duties, such as through the extension of Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR) and Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR) to fathers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These schemes aim to encourage married women to continue working after childbirth, rather than provide general assistance to families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Families can benefit from other parenthood-related tax benefits, such as Qualifying Child Relief (QCR) and Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She also suggested that exclusive, non-transferrable parental leave be equalised between mothers and fathers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin stated that more exclusive paternity leave would be a strong signal, so that couples do not have to make tough decisions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng has also asked for a phased increase of paternity leave.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We know that children benefit from having involved fathers who are committed to their growth and development.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Today, fathers can already benefit from a series of leave enhancements made over the years.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Most recently, in 2017, we made the second week of paternity leave mandatory and shared parental leave was extended from one to four weeks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In total, fathers may take up to eight weeks of leave in the child’s first year, which they can use to spend time with both mother and child.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Over the years, paternity leave take-up has increased markedly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The introduction of GPPB is also a recognition of the Government's support for fathers who may be in less conventional working arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Despite these improvements, there is still some way to go.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I encourage more fathers to take their leave, but in order for fathers to do so, mindsets will have to shift and this can only happen over time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: One key contributor is whether fathers feel supported in the workplace and I encourage employers to implement more family-friendly practices like flexible working arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I assure Mr Louis Ng that MSF is often in close consultation with our community partners, such as the Families for Life or the Centre for Fathering, which drives the Dads for Life movement to encourage active fathering.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF takes the building of strong marriages and families seriously.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to push through this effort with our partners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng have asked for leave to be extended to couples who suffer miscarriages, as they will need to recover.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng, in particular, suggested that the Government could extend partial reimbursement to employers who provide leave benefits to couples who have a miscarriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I understand the Members' concern, as miscarriages are unfortunate events.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Today, working mothers who need to recuperate after a miscarriage are given medical leave.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These working mothers can also use their annual leave and some companies may also offer compassionate leave.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Bill takes reference from the Registration of Births and Deaths Act (RBDA) in defining a stillbirth as one occurring after the 28th week of pregnancy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As the Member is aware, the new RBDA was recently passed in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When the new RBDA comes into effect, the CDCA will also take on this interpretation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I agree with Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Yip Hon Weng that families require further support as they recover physically and emotionally from the loss of a child, whether through a stillbirth or a miscarriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We encourage families in need to seek help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Families may also approach Family Service Centres for support on socio-emotional issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To the Member's query as to whether an adoptive father qualifies for leave and benefits, currently, paternity leave applies to both biological and adoptive fathers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also suggested that more leave, above and beyond the current maternity leave provisions, could be extended to parents who have stillbirths.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some companies may also offer compassionate leave over and beyond these entitlements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Joan Pereira has also called for additional leave for parents with multiple births, as they may face increased caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked that we consider giving parents full flexibility to share parental leave.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While more leave that could be flexibly used could be useful, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin has rightly pointed out that there are associated costs in implementing family-friendly practices and a practical approach must be taken and we have to be mindful that we do not, inadvertently, affect parents' employability if they are absent from work for an extended period of time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Employers face manpower and operational demands and these must be calibrated alongside the need to support working parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I would like to reassure Members that I know where they are coming from and I do know that they want to support parents as much as they can.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Any increase in leave provisions, however, will have to be considered carefully, especially in periods of business uncertainty.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I agree with Ms Joan Pereira that flexibility and mutual understanding between employers and employees are key.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Flexible workplace arrangements (FWAs), which contribute to a family-friendly work environment are more sustainable and can be tailored to a parent's own needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat suggested that more could be done to reward companies that are pro-family.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Today, the Tripartite Standards on FWAs, on Work-Life Harmony and on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs recognise progressive companies that support their employees, including those with caregiving responsibilities, to manage both their work and personal needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Employers who adopt these Standards can use the Tripartite Standard (TS) Logo to distinguish themselves as employers of choice.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: COVID-19 has also helped create momentum for the use of FWAs, as companies realised that FWAs could be implemented effectively and efficiently as we transition into the new normal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We encourage more employers to come on board and the Government will work with the tripartite partners to look into other ways to have FWAs become a norm at workplaces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As to the Member's suggestion on introducing grants or funding schemes to employers who have demonstrated their commitment to fostering family-friendly workplaces in Singapore, we thank him for his suggestion and we will review this further.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng has also asked if a public consultation was done for this Bill and to share the reasons why it was not done, given that many could have given constructive feedback to refine the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First, the process of consultation is not a one-off event.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Many Members today have given their feedback on the various schemes under the purview of the CDCA over the years, both formally and informally.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also debated vigorously on the merits of various support schemes that families can access.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, we have regular touchpoints with parents and employers through our community partners and tripartite partners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I assure the Member that we have always adopted a listening posture and are receptive to feedback.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Bill is, therefore, a culmination of many feedback cycles, instead of a single consultation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Second, most will benefit from this round of amendments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is the result of the Government stepping up to provide additional support that accrues directly to parents and employers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng raised a question that is close to my heart: how do we measure the success of our efforts to create a Singapore that is Made for Families?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Statistics like the take-up rate of various leave schemes, though useful, provide a limited understanding of the daily lives of families and their needs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I can assure the Member that this question preoccupies our minds and, MSF, together with the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD), will strive to continue to keep our ear to the ground.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, they do not and should not function in isolation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will only be possible with the help of our immediate and extended families, employers and community partners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF will continue to do our best to ensure that our policies build a better future for Singapore, anchored by strong families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The Minister of State has shared that we cannot give the cash component of the Baby Bonus to singles or unweds because it is part of the Marriage and Parenthood package, the key word being "marriage".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I just want to point out that the CDA component of the Baby Bonus is also part of the Marriage and Parenthood package, but we do give it to the single unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, why can we not just extend the other portion of the Baby Bonus to the single unweds?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Six hundred dollars for someone caring for a newborn!

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think this cash that many of us are pushing for is not a luxury for them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It really is a lifeline and I hope MSF will reconsider this policy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I have mentioned, there have been several reviews on our Marriage and Parenthood Packages.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned, there are certain Government policies that encourage parenthood within marriage; the Baby Bonus cash gift is one such benefit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But again, I would like to remind our Members that I have listed a whole series of benefits that have been equalised for children of both unwed as well as wedded parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I hope that we can look at this holistically.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But again, as I have said, we constantly review our Marriage and Parenthood Packages and will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, you have a clarification?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And I thank the Minister of State Ms Sun Xueling for the response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I hope that she would be able to clarify: in her explanation about CPF and CDA having different objectives, which she explained at length and, to be clear, I absolutely do not contest, it still remains unanswered why one qualifies for legislative protection of returns but the other does not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Since we are doing clarifications, I should clarify myself that my reference to legislative protections for returns to CPF should not be construed as a ringing endorsement of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, it is more short-term in nature because they can go and withdraw from the CDA bank account to defray those expenses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is different from the CPF, which is locked in for a longer period of time.      .
